name: Ethan Anand
life: “I still remember meeting the client who never laughed on the afternoon shift.” Sunday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Ethan pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I usually get the cheerful version of our client. The afternoon carer introduced me to her furious version.
appearance: Out of work clothes, look for an olive canvas jacket and one cuff folded back twice. Ethan has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. Ethan touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word during a conversation.
personality: Ethan has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Ethan knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To hear the client's afternoon point of view.
family: Kai Gross is Ethan’s older cousin. Ethan brings a spare shopping bag. Kai chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A tenant who stays*, Kai says, “I planted a tree after each miscarriage. I never told the man who owns the ground.”
connections: Nathan Neal (care colleague). The carer who stays for breakfast finally hears the version of the client known on afternoons.

reactions.situation: A supervisor objects to the overlap
reactions.response: Ethan records what the overlap let the client do before judging its cost.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Ethan writes down the shift time accurately, then helps them explain the circumstances without having to tell the whole room.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Ethan asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
